narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Late-Night Broadcast"**

Muzix is a station on the air after midnight, and it restyles itself for every show. The top bar is the transmitter: the striped logo, then an italic ticker that announces what's on ("Now playing", "On air", or a quote between shows). The footer is the station's status line, set in tiny spaced-out monospace: the host name, track counts, the skin on air, a fullscreen hint. Between them sits the screen itself, a thin rounded frame floating on a nebula backdrop, with the library to its left and what's playing to its right. When the music changes genre, the whole station re-dresses for the show: death metal brings bone and blood with blackletter type, a chiptune brings CRT scanlines and pixel type, jazz brings Blue Note duotones.

The house look, used when no skin is on air, is night-time warm: Bone text on Midnight Navy, Marigold for whatever is live, Vermilion for the one thing to do next, and a soft nebula of jade, marigold and vermilion glow behind everything. Headings are loud (heavy condensed capitals); everything around them is quiet. The layout follows Spotify's arrangement, so nobody has to learn where things are; the personality lives in the type, the colour, the skins and the broadcast furniture (ticker, stripes, mono labels, status line).

Density is a listener's density, not a dashboard's: generous page margins, large covers, and lists that breathe at about 60px per row. The interface is built to be left running on a screen as much as to be operated.
keyCharacteristics: Every colour, font and corner comes from role variables that the 98 colour schemes and 25 genre skins swap out. Nothing in a component is hard-wired to the house palette.
Heavy uppercase display type for headings; tiny spaced monospace for labels and status; a plain sans for everything you read or press.
The frame: one 1px hairline panel with 14px corners, inset 8px from the window, holding the page; the side docks share its edge.
Broadcast furniture: the ticker in the top bar, the footer status line, the five-colour stripes.
Quiet, precise controls: small outlined buttons, round icon buttons, pill chips. They never outshout the headings or the cover art.

rules.name: The Roles-Not-Hex Rule
rules.body: Components take colour only from the role variables (`--bg`, `--surface`, `--text`, `--primary`, `--secondary`, their derived shades and `--stripe-1…6`). A hex code in a component breaks 122 themes at once. The one exception is the bento tiles, which keep a fixed dark plate (#10131c with #f6f1e7 text) under their duotone photos.

rules.name: The 4.5 Floor Rule
rules.body: Dim and faint text are the text colour faded toward the background, but only as far as still reads at 4.5:1 on both the background and the surface. Text on an accent is near-black or white, whichever reads better. Red error text moves toward white (or black, on light schemes) until it reads at 4.5:1, and a red notice's colour is nudged until its text does. When a scheme's own text is weaker than that, dim and faint text stay at the text colour.

rules.name: The On-Air Rule
rules.body: Marigold means "this is live" (playing, selected, focused, on). Vermilion means "do this". Neither is used as decoration on a quiet surface.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: The display font shouts and the monospace whispers; the UI font carries everything in between. Nothing else gets a fourth voice.

rules.name: The Kicker Placement Rule
rules.body: Kickers sit above page titles and section titles, as they do now. They never go on cards, rows, dialogs or controls.

rules.name: The Frame Rule
rules.body: On desktop, every page lives inside the frame. On phones there is no frame, by the owner's decision.

rules.name: The Flat Studio Rule
rules.body: Panels, rows, chips and buttons never cast shadows. If something needs to look raised, it is either a cover or a floating layer.

dos: **Do** take every colour, font and radius from the theme variables (`--bg`, `--surface`, `--text`, `--primary`, `--secondary`, `--font-display`, `--font-ui`, `--font-mono`, `--radius`, `--display-case`) so all 98 colour schemes and 25 genre skins work.

**Do** check new UI under the house scheme, a light skin (punk, classical, country, pop, comedy or kids) and a skin that decorates the frame (death metal's thorns, soundtrack's film strip, punk's tape).
**Do** keep pages inside the frame on desktop and edge to edge on phones.
**Do** size page content against the frame with container queries (`cqi`, `@container page`), not the window.

**Do** take dim, faint, on-accent and error text from the theme (`--text-dim`, `--text-faint`, `--on-primary`, `--on-secondary`, `--error-text`, and `--on-error` on `--error-solid`); never pick a text colour for an accent by hand.
**Do** keep controls quiet: 38px buttons with 12px labels, 32px icon buttons, outlines before fills, and one Vermilion action per view.
**Do** keep the broadcast furniture on every desktop screen: the striped logo, the ticker, the footer status line.
donts: **Don't** hard-code the house hex values in a component; the one sanctioned exception is the bento tiles' fixed dark plate.
**Don't** put a frame, border or rounded panel around the page on phones.
**Don't** add shadows to the frame, docks, rows, chips or buttons; shadows are for covers and floating layers.
**Don't** add kickers to cards, rows, dialogs or controls; they belong above page and section titles.
**Don't** use the display font or heavy capitals for body copy, or monospace for prose.
**Don't** add gradient, chrome or textured text outside a skin's headline treatment; the house display type is solid Bone and Marigold.
**Don't** let Marigold decorate quiet surfaces; it marks what is live, selected or focused.
